notes: Pin it in 👋🏻│welcome. Templates: BLHA Talking Head, 01 Brand Kit (lower third: [YOUR NAME] · COMMISSIONER at 0:03, end card at the close).
Hey, I'm [your first name], the Commissioner of the BLHA, and welcome to the league.
You're one of twelve founding owners. That means the record book starts with you: the first champion, the first trade of the year, the first banner in the rafters.

Here's how it works. Fantrax is where the hockey happens: your roster, your lineup, trades and scoring. Discord is the league office and the clubhouse. That's where you'll find the news, the votes, the rulings and a lot of chirping.

Before anything else, read the Constitution. It's short, and joining the league means you've agreed to it. Then pay your dues through Fantrax Treasurer, name your franchise and say hello in the GM lounge.
If you have a question about a rule, ask in rules-questions. If it's private, open a ticket and it comes straight to me.
Build something you're proud of. Trade often. Set your lineup. I'll see you at the draft.

rows: Server with every category collapsed
This is a two-and-a-half-minute tour of the BLHA server. Every category has one job.
🏛️ LEAGUE OFFICE

The League Office is official business. Start in welcome, read the Constitution, and keep an eye on announcements and the league calendar. The ledger shows dues and prizes, league-voting is where formal votes happen, and hall-of-champions and league-records keep the history.
📰 THE WIRE
The Wire is NHL news, posted automatically: breaking news, injuries, transactions and prospects. Talk about any of it in news-desk.
💼 GENERAL MANAGERS
General Managers is the clubhouse. GM lounge for league talk, game-day for live games and starting goalies, chirps-and-memes for trash talk, and off-topic and media for everything else.
🔄 TRADE CENTER
In the Trade Center, post who you'll move in trade-block and what you need in looking-to-acquire. Every finished trade lands in completed-trades.
🌱 SCOUTING and 💰 WAIVER WIRE
Scouting is one forum for every prospect. Waiver Wire covers FAAB strategy and who to watch before claims run.
🏆 LEAGUE COMPETITION

League Competition runs itself: the live scoreboard, standings, the Monday recap, the playoff race and the brackets. Opt in to lineup alerts and you'll get a heads-up when a reserve plays and a starter doesn't.
🧑🏻‍⚖️ COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE

Questions go to the Commissioner's Office. Ask about a rule in rules-questions, open a private ticket in open-a-ticket and read official rulings in rulings-log. The owner handbook has the week-to-week basics.
🎯 DRAFT CENTER and 🏒 FRANCHISE HQ
The Draft Center comes alive around each draft. Franchise HQ is yours: the franchise directory, your team's news and your roster.
Channels & Roles
Last thing: pick your notification roles under Channels and Roles, so you only get pinged for what you care about.

title: The Constitution in 3 minutes (explainer)
notes: Post it in 📜│constitution under the eight messages, and in 📖│owner-handbook. Templates: BLHA Explainer, 11 Explainer Cards.
rows: Title: THE CONSTITUTION IN 3 MINUTES
This is the BLHA Constitution in three minutes. It's the short version. The full text in the constitution channel always wins.
Card: ROSTER

Every team has twenty active players: three centers, three left wings, three right wings, three forwards of any kind, six defensemen and two goalies. Add six reserves, ten minor-league spots and up to five IR spots.
Card: MINORS

A minor-leaguer has to be 25 or younger on the NHL's opening night, as Fantrax calculates it. Skaters stay eligible through 100 career NHL games, goalies through 50. When Fantrax flags a player, you have three days to move him.
Card: LINEUPS AND GOALIES
Lineups are daily. Each player locks about a minute before his game. Only four goalie starts count each week, and eight across the two-week Championship.
Card: WAIVERS

Free agents come through FAAB only. You get a thousand dollars of FAAB each season. Bids are hidden, a tie goes to the earliest bid, and claims run every day around 11 a.m. Eastern. You get five pickups a week.
Card: TRADES
Trades are unlimited, with no votes and no vetoes. You can trade players, draft picks and this season's FAAB. The deadline is 11:59 p.m. Eastern on the Sunday that ends Week 20.
Card: PAY FIRST, THEN TRADE
One rule to remember: before you trade away a future first- or second-round pick, your dues have to be paid through that pick's season. If they aren't, the trade gets reversed.
Card: PLAYOFFS
Six teams make the playoffs. The top two get byes, the bracket reseeds every round and the Championship lasts two weeks. The other six play a consolation bracket for a fifty-dollar FAAB bonus.
Card: DRAFT ORDER
The Annual Draft is five rounds every summer. The six non-playoff teams pick first, ordered by Potential Points, so benching your stars won't move you up.
Card: MONEY

Dues are a hundred and fifty dollars a season. Most of it goes to prizes: six-fifty for the champion, three-fifty for the runner-up, one-fifty for third and two hundred for the Presidents' Trophy. Two hundred a season builds the Dynasty Pot.
Card: CHANGING THE RULES
Rule changes happen in the offseason only, and they need eight of the twelve franchise votes.
End card
That's the league. Read the whole thing once. It's shorter than you think.

title: How scoring works (60 seconds, explainer)
notes: Post it in 📜│constitution and 🔎│scouting. Templates: BLHA Explainer, 11 Explainer Cards.
rows: Title: HOW SCORING WORKS
Here's how a BLHA team scores points.
Card: SKATERS with every value

For skaters, a goal is five points and an assist is two point nine seven. A shot on goal is point five three, a block point four four and a hit point one four. Each penalty minute costs point three six.
Card: GOALIES with every value
Goalies get five points just for starting, point five six for every save, and lose five for every goal against. A goalie who scores or sets one up gets the same points as a skater.
So two goals, an assist, five shots and a hit is a fifteen-point-eight night. Thirty saves on thirty-two shots is eleven-eighty. And a goalie who gives up six on twenty-five shots costs you fourteen.
Card: NOT SCORED
There are no points for wins, shutouts, plus-minus or power-play bonuses. Shots, blocks and hits matter more than you'd think.
End card
Nothing to say.

title: Where the money goes (45 seconds, explainer)
notes: Post it in 💰│league-ledger. Templates: BLHA Explainer, 11 Explainer Cards.
rows: Title: WHERE THE MONEY GOES
Every franchise pays a hundred and fifty dollars a season. Twelve franchises make eighteen hundred dollars, and here's where all of it goes.
Card: PRIZES
Six-fifty to the BLHA Champion, three-fifty to the runner-up, one-fifty for third place, and two hundred for the Presidents' Trophy, the best regular-season record.
Card: DYNASTY POT
Two hundred goes into the Dynasty Pot. The first franchise to win three championships in the same cycle takes all of it.
Card: RESERVE AND LEAGUE SERVICES
A hundred and fifty covers Fantrax Premium and other approved costs, and whatever's left joins the Dynasty Pot. The last hundred is the Commissioner's allocation for running the league.
Card: THE LEDGER
Every dollar is posted in the league ledger after each season.

Your roster in Fantrax, lineup editor open

Card: IF HE STOPS QUALIFYING
If Fantrax flags one as ineligible later, you have three days to promote, trade or drop him. Any illegal roster has to be fixed within twenty-four hours.

title: Placing a FAAB bid (60 seconds)

Bids are hidden and go up in one-dollar steps, and zero-dollar bids are allowed. If two bids tie, the one placed first wins.

title: Meet the League Bot (90 seconds, record once the bot is live)
rows: Title: THE LEAGUE BOT
The League Bot answers league questions right in Discord. It reads Fantrax and never changes anything there.
Typing /myteam
Slash myteam shows your roster counts, your picks, how far your dues are paid and this week's matchup. Only you see it.
Typing /rule prepayment
Slash rule shows any section of the Constitution. Slash deadlines lists the next dates.
Typing /minor and a name
Slash minor checks whether a player is minor-eligible.
Typing /tradecheck
Slash tradecheck checks a trade against the rules before you send it: picks, prepayment, roster limits and the deadline. It never grades a trade.
🏒│game-day: Pick'em and BLHA Bucks
In game-day there's a weekly Pick'em and BLHA Bucks, a play-money sportsbook on our matchups. You can't bet on your own.
🗳️│league-voting

title: How the Annual Draft order works (60 seconds, explainer)
notes: Post it in 📢│draft-announcements once the playoffs end, and pin it in 📖│owner-handbook. Templates: BLHA Explainer, 11 Explainer Cards, bed-tutorial-loop.
rows: Title card: THE ANNUAL DRAFT ORDER
Every summer the BLHA holds a five-round draft. Here's how the order is set.
Card: 5 ROUNDS · LINEAR
It's linear, not a snake. Whatever pick you have in round one, you have in every round.
Card: PICKS 1.01 TO 1.06
The first six picks go to the six teams that missed the playoffs. They're ordered by Potential Points, lowest first.
Card: POTENTIAL POINTS
Potential Points is what your team would have scored with its best possible lineup every week, from your active and reserve players.
Card: BENCHING DOESN'T HELP
So sitting your stars to lose doesn't move you up. Your best lineup counts either way.
Card: 1.07 AND 1.08
Picks seven and eight go to the two quarterfinal losers, lower seed first.
Card: 1.09 TO 1.12
Then fourth place, third place, the runner-up, and the champion picks last.
Card: CONSOLATION
The consolation bracket doesn't change the order. Its winner gets fifty dollars of extra FAAB instead.
End card: DRAFT ORDER · 📋│draft-results
The full order goes up in draft-results as soon as the Championship is final.

title: Awards Night host script (about 20 minutes, live or recorded)
notes: Run it in a voice channel or record it and post it in 📢│announcements. It follows the Awards Night program, in the same order. Templates: BLHA Awards Night, 10 Awards Night (one card per award: name, the top three with points, winner), bed-awards-loop under the talking and sfx-reveal on every winner. Tally the 5-3-1 votes from 🗳️│league-voting before you start.
1. Welcome

Good evening, and welcome to the [year] BLHA Awards Night. I'm [name], your Commissioner. Tonight we close the book on the [year] season: the champions, the money and the five awards you voted on. Let's start with a look back.
(Play the Season in Review.)
2. The season's honors. Read each one and pause for the card.
• The consolation champion, with fifty dollars of extra FAAB next season: [team].
• The Presidents' Trophy, for the best regular-season record, and two hundred dollars: [team], at [record].
• Third place, and one hundred and fifty dollars: [team].
• The runner-up, and three hundred and fifty dollars: [team].
• And your [year] BLHA Champion, with six hundred and fifty dollars and a banner in the hall of champions: [team]. (Let the sting play. Give the champion's owner the floor if it's live.)
3. The owners' awards. Before the first one, say this:

Every franchise got one ballot: a first, second and third choice for each award, worth five, three and one points. Nobody could vote for their own franchise, their own pickups, or a trade they were part of. Bust of the Year is the one exception. These awards are for bragging rights. No money, no picks.

Then, for each award, the same three lines: "The nominees for [award] are [third place], [second place] and [first place]." Pause. "And the winner, with [points] points, is... [winner]." Then one sentence on why.
• Bust of the Year. "We start with the one nobody wants: the season's biggest letdown."
• Comeback Franchise (from the league's second season on). "The biggest climb in the standings from last season."
• Waiver Steal of the Year. "The best pickup off the wire."
• Trade of the Year. "The best deal of the season. The two teams in it couldn't vote for it."
• GM of the Year. "And the last award of the night: the best job running a franchise this season."
If an award is tied after first-place votes, say: "It's a tie, so the award is shared," and read both.
4. The Dynasty Pot
The Dynasty Pot now stands at [balance]. The first franchise to win three championships in this cycle takes all of it. [Team] has [number]. (If nobody has two: "Nobody has two yet. It's wide open.")
5. What's next

The Season Ledger goes up in league-ledger within thirty days, with every dollar in and out. Trading reopens the day after the Stanley Cup Final. The Annual Draft starts two to three weeks after the NHL Entry Draft, and dues are due before it. The dates are on the league calendar. Thank you all for a great season. See you at the draft.
